name: As found, as left
oneLine: A two-column specimen strip that calibrates the portfolio itself: the same claim AS FOUND (a hollow bar with one end, `U = —` beneath it) and AS LEFT (a serifed bracket with two ends, real digits, a gold nominal tick only where the source is checkable).
threeSecondRead: Left: a bar. It has one end, no unit, and `U = —` under it — the certificate's own notation for "this row states no uncertainty", which in metrology means it is not a measurement.
Right: the same three claims with two ends each — a serifed bracket, real digits (P95 < 200 ms · 10,000+ devices), and one gold tick sitting on the only figure whose source you can ring up.
The bottom right row has no tick, no bracket that closes, and a 45° hatch reading LIMITED CALIBRATION — NO CERTIFICATE ISSUED. That row is why the two above it are believable.
form:
A single inline SVG figure, `viewBox="0 0 1120 300"`, wrapper `aspect-ratio: 1120/300; contain: layout paint`. Every element is `line`, `polyline`, `rect`, `text` or `pattern` — deliberately **zero `<path>`**, so `TC-BENCH-01` (`#skills svg path` count 20) and `TC-BENCH-02` (17 gold-stroked paths) keep passing untouched. `vector-effect="non-scaling-stroke"`, `shape-rendering="crispEdges"` on rules, verticals at `n + 0.5`.

Four bands. Header y 56–96: mono 10px/.12em uppercase column heads `AS FOUND` (x 276) sub `SELF-REPORTED`, and `AS LEFT` (x 512) sub `MEASURED · WITH ITS CONDITIONS`; a right-aligned title block at x 1096 reading `CERT 16b856c0` / `SCALE 1:1 · 17 ROWS · 13 SOURCES` from `cvFingerprint.short`, `capabilities.length`, `sources.length`. Under the AS LEFT head, mono 9px `--ink-300`: `POSITION IS NOT A QUANTITY — THE DIGITS ARE THE MEASUREMENT`. Two full-height divider rules at x 252 and x 488, `--ink-500` 0.5px; the second is the substitution seam the eye crosses once per row.

Three rows, centres y 138 / 196 / 254, labelled at x 220 right-aligned in `--font-body` 0.82rem `--mist-200` with the real `short` strings: *Real-time telemetry*, *LLM eval & guardrails*, *AWS & GCP certification*.

**AS FOUND cell — identical in all three rows.** One `polyline` `452,R-9 276,R-9 276,R+9 452,R+9`: top, left edge, bottom. The right side is never drawn. `--ink-500`, 0.75px, butt caps, miter joins, no fill. Beneath at y R+22, mono 10px `--ink-300`: `U = —`. No number, no tick, no unit. Three completely different claims drawn identically — that identity *is* the refutation.

**AS LEFT cell.** (a) range-frame hairline at y R+11 spanning only the bracket, `--ink-500` 0.5px; (b) the bracket: horizontal `line` x 512→812, `--mist-200` 1.25px, with two 12-unit vertical butt-capped serifs at each end — the Caliper's jaw geometry at scale; (c) nominal tick, vertical 20 units, **1.5px**: `var(--gold)` on row 1 (ANZ, a programme you can ring), `var(--white)` on row 2 (measured against a simulated budget — never gold), absent on row 3; (d) tolerance limit: dashed vertical `--mist-400` 0.75px `stroke-dasharray="3 4"`, x 884, mono 9px head `TL 200 ms` / `SCOPE LIMIT`. Row 2's right serif lands at x 868 — sixteen units short of the limit, labelled `CONDITIONAL`. That is ILAC-G8's guard band, and it is exactly that row's real caveat.

**Row 3** replaces all of it: a `rect` 512→1096 filled `url(#cal-hatch)` (a `pattern` of one `line`, 6px pitch, 45°, `--ink-500`), two dashed serifs with no horizontal member between them — arms that do not meet — and centred mono 10px `LIMITED CALIBRATION — NO CERTIFICATE ISSUED`.

Under-labels, mono 10px at y R+26, verbatim from `skills.ts`: `P95 < 200 ms · 10,000+ concurrent devices · ANZ Banking Group` / `−38% error-budget breaches · simulated budget, not live traffic · Independent · aether-job-career-agent` / `studying · no certificate issued · no source`.
motion:
One-shot `IntersectionObserver` at `threshold: 0.15`, `disconnect()` on first hit — the exact block at `Bench.tsx:194-206`. Two flags, `drawn` then `settled`, as Bench does. Adds one token to `globals.css`: `--motion-ease-mechanical: cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)` — a caliper that overshoots is a broken caliper, so `--motion-ease-emphasized` is reserved here for ink arriving, never for the mechanism.

Beat 1, 0–560 ms — the three AS FOUND polylines draw. `pathLength="1"`, `stroke-dasharray: 1; stroke-dashoffset: 1 → 0`, 560 ms `--motion-ease-mechanical`, `animation-delay: calc(var(--i) * 34ms)` set inline as `style={{ '--i': i }}` (the Bench idiom, and `--i` is invisible to the token gate).

Beat 2, 560–1400 ms — per row the bracket's horizontal member rules in left→right (`pathLength=1` dash trace, 620 ms `--motion-ease-emphasized` — printing, so a soft settle is right), then the two serifs and the nominal tick fade `opacity 0 → 1` over 160 ms. 34 ms stagger, total stagger capped at 102 ms. The gold tick on row 1 is the last mark to arrive in the beat.

Beat 3, 1400–2100 ms — row 3 only. The hatch `rect` wipes in on `clip-path: inset(0 100% 0 0) → inset(0 0 0 0)`, 520 ms `--motion-ease-mechanical` (a 584×32 box: paint cost is trivial and it runs once), then the dashed open arms and the `LIMITED CALIBRATION` text fade over 200 ms. The gap arrives **last**, never first.

`settled` flips at 2220 ms from a timeout computed off the stagger total (`120 + 2*34 + 2100`), and `.settled *` sets `animation: none`, so a resize, a container-query re-evaluation or a tab return can never replay the explainer under the reader. `will-change: opacity` on at most the two traced groups, added on `drawn`, removed on `settled`. Dimming, if ever added, uses `stroke-opacity` — a running animation on `opacity` beats any selector's specificity (`Bench.module.css:92-102`).
states:
**Reduced motion.** Motion is authored as the enhancement, not the override: base CSS *is* the settled frame, and the whole animation block lives inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`, so a missed selector fails static rather than animated. JS mirrors `Bench.tsx:189-193` — `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches` sets `drawn = true` at mount without waiting for the observer. The global kill-switch at `globals.css:691-699` is therefore harmless. No canvas, so `TC-CINE-04` (zero `canvas` under reduce) is unaffected. The static frame is the canonical image; the animation is only its unfolding.

**390px.** Below 900px the figure refuses to compress the two-column comparison and instead drops to two rows — *Real-time telemetry* (gold tick, sourced) and *AWS & GCP certification* (hatched, open) — sourced first, gap second, preserving the pratfall ordering. `viewBox="0 0 358 250"`, AS FOUND and AS LEFT stacked as two sub-rows per claim with the column heads inline above each, bracket width 220, TL at x 340, under-labels wrapped across two `<text>` lines at mono 9px. Row 2 is dropped; it is already in the table below verbatim. No diagram pretending to be readable at 390px (`Bench.module.css:283-284`).

**Keyboard / screen reader.** The SVG is `aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"` (Bench's choice — keeps the axe sweep at `accessibility.spec.ts:124` clean) and adds no focusable node, no `role="status"` (`TC-SKILL-07` requires exactly one live region in `#skills`), and no `progress` / `meter` / `[role=progressbar]` (`TC-SKILL-03` requires zero). The `<figure>` carries a real `<figcaption>` plus a visually-hidden `<ul>` — reusing `Caliper.module.css`'s `.gloss` clip pattern — that states each specimen in words, and says explicitly that the left-hand bar is an illustration of a convention this page rejects, not a claim about him. That sentence is what a future "tidy-up" is most likely to delete, so it gets its own test.

**No JS.** Everything is server-rendered markup with fixed `viewBox` coordinates — nothing here is measured from layout, unlike the Bench's wires — so the un-hydrated first paint is the complete, correct figure. The wrapper's `aspect-ratio` reserves the box before hydration; CLS contribution is zero and LCP is unaffected (no raster, no font subset, ~4 kB gzipped inline).
coherence:
**Where it goes.** Between `<header>` and `<Bench />` in `Skills.tsx:88-102`, and it **absorbs the lede**. `skillsContent.lede`'s first two sentences are deleted — the metaphor is now drawn, so explaining it in prose is the split-attention failure the section currently commits. The third sentence becomes the `<figcaption>`, promoted to heading weight in `--font-heading` 1.05rem and rewritten so its first two words carry it (NN/g layer-cake): *"Nothing here is self-rated."* Everything below is unchanged; the Bench and the table keep their exact contract.

**Devices it extends.** The bracket-with-serifs is the Caliper's own geometry drawn at figure scale, so the mark the site asks a reader to learn is taught here in its three states — closed on a source, closed but grey, open over hatch — before the table asks them to read it. The hatch is `Caliper.module.css`'s existing 45° `open` fill, expressed as an SVG `pattern` (id `cal-hatch`, a literal string, not `useId` — React ids carry colons that are illegal inside `url(#…)`). Motion reuses Bench's `drawn`/`settled` two-flag shape and its `pathLength={1}` normalisation verbatim.

**Devices it deliberately avoids.** No dial, bezel, rotating ring or index-at-twelve — Compass owns those. No proportional bar on a shared axis, no decade gridlines, no axis ticks — Experience owns those, and this figure prints `POSITION IS NOT A QUANTITY` to disclaim the resemblance outright. No wires, rails or node-link graph — the Bench, forty pixels below, owns those. No box-and-arrow flow and no literal drawn caliper in a chart — Vitrine owns those. It spends only what the site's own collision map lists as unclaimed: the substitution gesture, the before/after swap, the side-by-side specimen, and the certificate title block.

**Gold.** Exactly one gold mark: a 1.5px vertical nominal tick, 20 units tall, on row 1 only, because `ANZ Banking Group` is a `programme` a stranger can ring up. Gold is a terminator, never a path — no gold axis, no gold bracket, no gold hatch, nothing gold that can be dragged along a length. Row 2 has a real measurement and stays white, because its evidence was taken against a simulated budget; row 3 has no tick at all. The palette rule and the lesson are the same rule. Written as `var(--gold)` (the `stopColor="var(--gold)"` idiom at `Bench.tsx:297` already passes), never as a hex, so gate 2's "gold only in `globals.css` and `lib/palette.ts`" holds. Styles live in a new `Specimen.module.css`, which gate 10 does not scan.
risks: Three identical hollow AS FOUND boxes can read as a loading skeleton rather than an argument, especially in the ~600 ms before beat 2 lands. Mitigation is the `U = —` label, which is present from the first frame and is text, not geometry — but if the label is ever shrunk below 10px or dropped on mobile, the whole left column becomes meaningless furniture.

`POSITION IS NOT A QUANTITY — THE DIGITS ARE THE MEASUREMENT` is the honest thing to print, and it is also a disclaimer that could read as an excuse for a drawing that does not encode anything. If a reader parses it as "this diagram is decorative", the figure has argued against itself. It survives only because the topology it *does* encode — one end vs two ends vs arms that never meet, and where the gold tick sits — is genuinely data-derived.

It is a table-shaped object sitting above a table, with a network diagram between them. Three grid-like artefacts in one section risks reading as repetition rather than as specimen → chain → record. If it does, the fix is to cut the figure to two rows on desktop as well, not to restyle it.

`Skills.tsx:31-34` states in the source that motion here is deliberately nil, as a contrast with the sixteen-year scrub in the section before. A 2.2 s explainer contradicts that written intent. It is defensible only as a single once-only gesture in the header zone that terminates in `animation: none` — if it ever gains a hover state, a replay, or a second beat, the section's stated character is gone.

Between roughly 900px and 1120px the AS LEFT under-labels — `−38% error-budget breaches · simulated budget, not live traffic · Independent · aether-job-career-agent` is 96 characters — will collide with the title block or overflow the viewBox. SVG `<text>` does not wrap; each of those strings needs a hand-authored two-line break at that range, and that is the most likely place this ships broken.

Deleting two sentences from `skillsContent.lede` removes text from `#skills`; `TC-CINE-04` requires every section's `innerText` to exceed 200 characters under reduced motion. There is ample margin, but the figcaption and the visually-hidden specimen list must be real DOM text, not SVG-only labels, or the margin narrows.
whyBest:
Every other candidate has to *assert* that proficiency bars are worthless. This one makes it a consequence of a notation the reader can see being applied evenly to both objects. `U = —` is three characters, printed in the certificate's own dash-means-not-applicable convention, and it does the entire job: a measurement without a stated uncertainty is not a measurement, so the bar is not a claim, so there is nothing to grade. The reader never has to accept an argument — they watch the same rule get applied twice and see one side come up empty.

It is also the only angle where the palette rule and the pedagogy are the same rule. Gold lands on one 1.5px tick, on the one row whose source is a phone call away; the row with a real measured number and a simulated environment stays white; the row with nothing stays hatched and open. A reader who learns nothing else learns *gold means someone else can check this* — which is the one convention the site asks them to carry into the next four screens.

And it clears every hard gate without a workaround rather than in spite of one: no `<path>` element, so the two bench tests that count paths in `#skills` are untouched; no new hex, no new colour-family token, no `role="status"`, no `progress`/`meter`, no canvas, no measured geometry, a reserved aspect-ratio box, and a static frame that is the canonical image rather than a degraded fallback. The three-second read survives a 200px greyscale screenshot with the motion switched off: one shape with one end, one shape with two, one shape whose arms never meet.
